constraints: Extract CommonMark links/images/references in document order without rendering, fetching, or reading destination contents. Decode Markdown entities and percent escapes exactly once. Incomplete checks must fail visibly.

Developer tooling on Python 3.9/3.13, Linux/macOS/Windows, including offline hash-locked installation. Small adversarial inputs must not silently omit links. No product runtime, hardware, hard-real-time or total-memory qualification is in scope.
comparison: Marko 2.2.4: historical bounded probes exceeded a 3-second subprocess budget for 32,128,256 nested quotes (79,271,527 bytes). Normal-case parity alone did not establish acceptable pathological behavior. Preserve these failures.

markdown-it-py: documented block/inline token API supports extraction without HTML rendering. Both 3.0.0 and 4.2.0 were executed. Default maxNesting silently omitted nested links in the saved 3.0.0 probe; explicit guards are necessary. The modified parser retains 32/63 nested quote links and explicitly rejects the boundary at 64.

Mistune: official API exposes an AST, making it a credible portable alternative. It was researched, not benchmarked in this correction; it has no demonstrated correctness/resource advantage over the tested adapter.

C cmark: official library exposes an AST and pathological-input tests. C MD4C: callback parsing can avoid a retained document AST. Both are credible native alternatives, not excluded by toolchain availability. They require a native distribution/binding plus the same application error mapping; neither was locally benchmarked or proved superior for this small offline checker. Reconsider them if total memory or sustained throughput becomes a required acceptance constraint.
rationale: MIGRATE Marko to markdown-it-py with explicit block/inline nesting rejection. The demonstrated small-input failure and the tested replacement behavior justify this incremental change; neither installed-tool convenience nor prior language choice is the basis.

Pin MIT universal wheels: markdown-it-py 3.0.0 for Python<3.10,4.2.0 otherwise; mdurl0.1.2. Wheel SHA256 values match requirements-links.lock. Retain the versioned report contract and shared worktree/public-tree adapter.
